item.title: [AI] Anthropic联合创始人回应METR报告
item.author: @Sam_McCandlish
item.description:
Anthropic联合创始人Sam McCandlish称已向METR提供未发布模型基准等内部数据供其独立评估；他认同AI在加速自家研究，并预告数周内将发布Anthropic自身的进度与安全举措分析。

@Sam_McCandlish · 赞 1617 · 转 128 · 浏览 173206

I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months. I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals. The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work. How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate. For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions. Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further. This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one. We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here. In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

item.title: [AI] 开源Hyperkernel加速GPU推理
item.author: @hyperstition_cc
item.description:
Hyperstition发布递归megakernel生成器Hyperkernel，称在DeepSeek/Kimi/GLM推理、预训练、机器人与FSD等11个领域达到SOTA，并开源相关megakernel与后续完整栈。

@hyperstition_cc · 赞 326 · 转 42 · 浏览 28696

We invented a recursive megakernel generator called Hyperkernel, the most complete solution to megakernels and GPU efficiency. Hyperkernel-generated megakernels achieve state of the art performance on 11 different domains: inference (DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM), pretraining (Qwen), hardware fault recovery, robotics (π₀-FAST, ACT) diffusion and real time world models (Matrix-Game), full self driving (OpenPilot), voice models (Moshi), genomics (Evo 2) and protein folding (ESMFold). All of this in a single kernel launch. For context, Hyperkernel generated fully optimized megakernels for robotics, genomics and voice in under 50 minutes, and doubled the efficiency for >5 models generally using only about 60-100 lines of code per megakernel. This speaks to the unparalleled standard for code quality in the automated generations. Our first release today open sources the megakernels themselves. Over the next couple weeks, we will release the entire Hyperkernel stack, along with the complete serving stack for Kimi and GLM (20-30% inference efficiency gains across all concurrencies). Out of the box GPU machinery performs terribly for unorthodox research. We built Hyperkernel only 20 days ago for internal use; but given its multi-modality, we have decided to open source it. Creative research should not be bottlenecked by the lack of dedicated infra teams. Hyperkernels offer a one stop shop infra stack for all research. We would love for the open source community to add to it :) GitHub repo: https://t.co/sfPt4S4BJN

item.title: [AI] StreamEval上线：38模型实时视频基准
item.author: @kimmonismus
item.description:
StreamEval公开实时视频AI基准，含300个15秒至5分钟脚本用例，覆盖Avatar、世界生成与视频编辑三类，并开源代码、数据集与评分协议。

@kimmonismus · 赞 82 · 转 7 · 浏览 7947

StreamEval is worth a look if you’re following real-time video AI. The paper reports results from 38 models. The benchmark contains 300 scripted test cases, each representing a session lasting from 15 seconds to five minutes. The leaderboard covers three categories: - Avatar: dialogue, performance and character consistency. - World generation: changing scenes while keeping them coherent. - Video editing: applying edits while preserving unaffected content. Across five tasks and ten metrics, it examines whether models follow requests, maintain visual quality and keep the scene consistent. That includes preserving an earlier edit when the next instruction arrives. The code, dataset, evaluation protocols and scoring rules are public. Researchers can inspect the test cases and run their own evaluations with the open-source implementation. The project brings together researchers affiliated with Tsinghua University, NVIDIA, Carnegie Mellon University, UC Berkeley, Princeton University, the National University of Singapore, and Reactor. If you’re building a video model, you can submit an API endpoint through “Evaluate your model”. The team reviews submissions for future evaluations. https://t.co/8AKklGVE2W Paper, code and dataset links below. #StreamEval #StreamEvalBenchmark #streamingvideo

Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️ We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and editing limit up to 15 seconds, and made updates to how scenes hold together over time. We've also given character speech an upgrade, reduced visual glitches like jump cuts, and made sure the model stays even truer to any reference assets you upload. So… what does all of that actually mean for you? It gives you more room to tell your story. With up to 15 seconds to work with, you have more flexibility to create what you need — videos look more cinematic and smooth, offering stronger consistency that keeps objects anchored from start to finish. And when characters speak, the dialogue sounds more fluid and natural. Creators and everyday users can start directing scenes and multi-turn edits in @FlowbyGoogle, generating 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids, or creating 15-second videos in the @GeminiApp. Plus, for developers and businesses building with the API, we've dropped the price by 30% from the previous generation, making it available at just $0.07 per second for 720p video.
